Package com.oracle.database.selectai.agent

Interface Tool

public interface Tool
Contract for Select AI agent tool lifecycle, description, and execution operations.

A tool is a database-side resource managed by the DBMS_CLOUD_AI_AGENT PL/SQL package. Tools expose callable functionality to agents or teams and may define an input schema.

A Tool instance can represent an existing database tool or be configured for creation. The name-only SelectAIAgent.tool(String) factory verifies that the tool exists and loads its metadata and attributes before returning. SelectAIAgent.listTools() also returns handles with loaded metadata and attributes. A handle configured for creation is obtained with SelectAIAgent.tool(String, ToolAttributes, String, ToolStatus).

A creation-configured handle retains its supplied attributes, description, and status without querying the database. Only such a handle can call create(); after creation succeeds, it becomes database-backed. enable(), disable(), drop(boolean), describe(), and run(String) require an existing database-side tool. Existing tools can update individual attributes with setAttribute(String, String) or multiple attributes with setAttributes(ToolAttributes); both operations reload the typed attributes after the database update succeeds.

Before creation, getStatus() and getToolAttributes() return the configured values. For a database-backed handle, each call to either method queries the database. getStatus() does not change the description returned by getDescription(). The description is supplied or loaded when the handle is initialized; getDescription() does not query the database. Use describe() to retrieve the database-generated tool definition.

Names and required Java arguments are checked locally. Loading metadata and executing tool operations require database access; the database checks privileges and validates tool attributes when they are submitted. The input supplied to run(String) must be a JSON payload accepted by the configured tool; the Java method checks only that it is not null or blank.

For a complete runnable example, see CreateToolSample source.

1.1.0

      boolean create() throws SelectAIException

    • drop

      boolean drop(boolean force) throws SelectAIException
      Drops this database-backed tool. When force is true, the operation may be retried after the handle has already been dropped; the database force-drop semantics determine the result. For a runnable example, see DropToolSample source.
      Parameters:
      force - database force-drop option
      Returns:
      true when the drop completes
      Throws:
      IllegalStateException - when force is false and this tool has not been created
      SelectAIException - when the database operation fails

    • run

      ToolRunResult run(String inputJson) throws SelectAIException
      Runs this tool with a JSON input payload.

      The SDK checks only that the payload is non-null and non-blank. The configured tool and database validate the JSON shape and its values. For a runnable example, see RunToolSample source.

      Parameters:
      inputJson - JSON input accepted by the configured tool
      Returns:
      typed result retaining the raw value returned by the database package
      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - when inputJson is null or blank
      IllegalStateException - when this tool has not been created
      SelectAIException - when the database operation fails

    • getToolName

      String getToolName()

      Returns:

    • getDescription

      String getDescription()
      Returns the description supplied or loaded when this handle was initialized. This method does not access the database and the value is not changed by getStatus(). For a runnable example, see LoadToolSample source.
      Returns:
      supplied or loaded tool description, or null when absent

    • getStatus

      ToolStatus getStatus() throws SelectAIException
      Returns the configured status before creation or the current database status for an existing tool. A pending tool with no configured status returns null. This method does not change the description. For a runnable example, see LoadToolSample source.
      Returns:
      configured or current tool status
      Throws:
      SelectAIException - when current tool metadata cannot be fetched

    • getToolAttributes

      ToolAttributes getToolAttributes() throws SelectAIException
      Returns tool attributes for this handle.

      For a database-backed tool, this method reloads the attributes from the database on each call and therefore can fail if the resource was deleted. For a creation-configured tool, it returns the configured attributes without querying the database. Built-in tool parameters use immutable ToolParams models. Input metadata is exposed as immutable ToolInput entries. Unknown parameter fields and newer database schemas are preserved. For a runnable example, see LoadToolSample source.

      Returns:
      current tool attributes for an existing tool, or configured attributes for a tool pending creation
      Throws:
      SelectAIException - when the tool no longer exists or current attributes cannot be fetched
